Definition: reflexive past of a compound of G575 and G2036; to say off for oneself, i.e. disown:--renounce.
BiblicalUsage: To renounce — Paul says we have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, refusing to walk in craftiness or handle God's word deceitfully. The word is a public disowning: those things are not mine any more.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that honesty in ministry starts here, with renouncing every shortcut that hides the truth.
